decisions.reason: Uses running-processes.txt to identify the dsh web host node.exe (PID 42432) as the process that loaded koffi.node, explains the OS keeps the loaded native binary locked until that process exits so npm's copyfile fails with EBUSY, and correctly separates the agent worker and the npm process (victim) from the lock holder.

Explains a browser refresh only reloads the SPA while the host process holding koffi keeps running, and gives an ordered procedure: stop the dsh host and dsh-related workers, verify none remain via tasklist, install from an external terminal, then restart and verify — without prescribing killing unrelated Node processes.

Grounded in npm-dist-tags.txt: the bare @deepseek-ai/dsh resolves through the latest dist-tag (0.1.1-rc.2) rather than preserving or advancing the installed 0.1.2-alpha.4, since alpha.5 lives only on the alpha tag; the unpinned install therefore silently downgraded the host.

Provides the exact pinned global install npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 together with the TUI plugin (exact-version pinned) after stopping the host, then dsh --version verification expecting alpha.5 and host restart with browser hard refresh; @alpha is mentioned only as a mutable alternative, not a substitute.

Advises README authors to pin the exact tested host version whenever a plugin install command also installs dsh (never a bare @deepseek-ai/dsh that follows latest), pin the plugin and state the tested host corridor, document the stop-before-upgrade requirement and post-install version verification.
